statement: Explain why and how central banks emerged, including war finance, note issue and the early central banks
Describe the histories of the Bank of England, Banque de France, Bundesbank, Bank of Italy and the Federal Reserve and the structure of the Federal Reserve
Explain how the functions of central banks evolved and the moral hazard of lender of last resort lending
Explain the reasons for the proliferation of central banks and the conflicting roles of the central bank
Explain the central bank role as banker to government, monetisation, debt management and its separation from monetary policy
Explain the central bank role as banker to banks and lender of last resort, including moral hazard
Explain the monetary policy function: sources of money supply change, base money and the money multiplier
Describe central bank digital currency and private digital currencies
Explain the monopoly of note issue and currency management
Explain payment and settlement systems and the models of central bank involvement
Explain how central banks maintain the internal value of currency, including the gold standard, the Great Depression and seigniorage
Explain inflation targeting, monetary targets and anchors and the prerequisites for inflation targeting
Explain the maintenance of the external value of currency, exchange rate regimes, the impossible trinity and the East Asian crisis
Explain the regulation and supervision of the financial system, the Basel framework and the structure of supervision
Explain the autonomy and independence of a central bank: the case for it, its three dimensions, the evidence and the time inconsistency problem
Explain the credibility and accountability of a central bank and the ways accountability is ensured
Explain transparency in central bank operations, the ELRIC framework and the key international standards and codes
Explain the conflict between monetary and fiscal policy: history, theory, global experience and the position of emerging economies
Describe the Indian experience with ad hoc Treasury Bills and Ways and Means Advances and the case for separating debt management from monetary policy
Identify the important committees listed in the courseware appendix and the subject each examined
Explain the genesis, objectives and functions of the IMF, the IBRD and the BIS
Explain the RBI instructions on the operations of Indian banks and AIFIs in IFSCs including GIFT City
Explain the central bank view of crypto currencies, including their genesis, nature and the case for and against a ban
Explain central bank digital currency, its design, features and the RBI pilots
Explain the findings of the RBI survey on climate risk and sustainable finance and the suggestions made to banks
Define the central banking glossary terms covered in the courseware appendix
Trace the evolution of the Reserve Bank from the Presidency Banks and Imperial Bank to the RBI Act, 1934 and nationalisation
Describe the developmental role of the Reserve Bank, the institutions it promoted and its response to bank nationalisation
Describe the development of payment and settlement systems and the cyber security framework
Explain the relationship of the Reserve Bank with the Government and the monetary-fiscal interface, including the end of automatic monetisation
Explain the structure and governance of the Reserve Bank in its early years
Describe the organisational developments in the Reserve Bank and the functions of its major departments
Explain the salient features of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934: chapters, Central Board, note issue, cash reserve and general provisions
Explain the need for and structure of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and its principal sections
Explain the external sector reforms, the enactment of FEMA and how it differs from FERA
Explain the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021: scope, maintainability, procedure, awards and appeals
Describe the financial sector reforms after 1991: banking, debt recovery, other segments and debt market reforms
Explain the approaches to financial regulation and the division of functions among Indian regulators
Describe the institutions set up by the Reserve Bank: NABARD, IDBI, DFHI, IRBI, UTI, EXIM Bank, NHB, CCIL, BCSBI, NPCI, NARCL and NaBFID
Explain the objectives of financial inclusion and the impediments to it (Information, Incentives and Transaction costs)
Explain the role, benefits and risks of mandates and subventions and the refinements made by the Reserve Bank
Explain how local institutions, small finance banks, credit information, land records, TReDS and digital payments support inclusion
Explain the issues in financial inclusion and their resolution: KYC, competition, flexibility, skilling and financial literacy
Describe the progress of financial inclusion, financial inclusion plans, business facilitators and correspondents, PMJDY and the link with monetary policy
Explain the goals, targets, indicators and objectives of monetary policy and the reconciliation of dual objectives
Explain rules versus discretion, the Friedman rule and the Taylor rule
Explain the instruments of monetary policy: Bank Rate, OMOs, the LAF corridor, CRR, SLR and selective credit controls
Explain the monetary policy transmission mechanisms and channels and their evaluation for emerging economies
Explain transparency, policy lags, the Indian policy process, the Monetary Policy Committee and flexible inflation targeting
Explain credit policy, how it differs from monetary policy, and how it is formulated in practice in India
Explain nominal versus real credit and the credit allocation mechanism across Government, industries, borrowers and sectors
Explain quantitative and selective credit controls, margin requirements and credit ceilings
Explain credit pricing from PLR to MCLR and the external benchmark recommendation, and the guidelines on digital lending
Explain monetary-fiscal relations in India: automatic monetisation, accommodative policy, the FRBM Act and the growth-inflation balance
Describe the finances of the Centre and States in 2020-21 and 2021-22 and the pandemic support measures
Explain the constitutional basis, functions and role of the Finance Commission
Explain the main recommendations of the Fifteenth Finance Commission on tax devolution, grants and fiscal rules
Explain liquidity management, the measures of banking system liquidity and the evolution of the LAF from 1999 to the 2011 Working Group
Explain the Patel Committee (2014) and Internal Working Group (2019) recommendations and the revised LAF framework and its operating principles
Describe the liquidity management measures during Covid-19 and the standing deposit facility introduced in April 2022
Explain the objectives and legal framework of foreign exchange reserve management and the credit, market, currency, interest rate and liquidity risks
Explain operational controls, transparency, the composition of reserves and the sources of variation, forward book and international investment position
Explain the adequacy of reserves, management of gold, the deployment of foreign currency assets and the IMF and SAARC arrangements
Explain why financial markets matter, the genesis of the Indian money market and the structure of the Indian financial markets
Explain the money market instruments and reforms: Treasury Bills, call money, repo, CBLO, commercial paper, certificates of deposit and derivatives
Explain the development of the Government securities market, the SLR history, the auction system, institutions and investor base
Explain the development of the foreign exchange market, the move from LERMS to a market determined rate, financial benchmarks and the LIBOR transition
Explain why banks are supervised, the CAMEL parameters and how the supervisor differs from the auditor
Describe the development of bank regulation in the UK, the US, Canada and other countries and the effect of the Great Depression
Explain the interaction between monetary policy and supervision: informational benefits, conflicts of interest and integration versus separation
Describe the genesis of bank regulation and supervision in India and why monetary policy and supervision are complementary in the Indian perspective
Trace the development of commercial bank regulation and supervision from 1950 to 1991 including inspections, nationalisation and the 1990s reforms
Explain prudential indicators, supervisory returns (structural liquidity, LCR, NSFR, gap and duration analysis) and risk management in banks
Explain the Covid-19 era regulatory measures, the Prompt Corrective Action framework, supervision of banks and the 2020 merger of public sector banks
Describe the recent performance and soundness of scheduled commercial banks and the Reserve Bank pandemic response
Explain the growth of the co-operative credit structure, the role of NABARD and the duality of control
Explain the strengthening of urban co-operative banks, their supervision, the 2020 Banking Regulation Act amendment and the amalgamation rules
Explain recent developments, the umbrella organisation, the four-tier framework, net worth and CRAR norms and the FSWM criteria for urban co-operative banks
Explain the 2008 crisis, the definitions of financial stability, the RBI's role and the post-crisis institutional framework
Explain risks to financial stability, early warning signals, the Financial Stability Report and the liquidity management principles
Explain the Board for Financial Supervision, CAMELS and CALCS, the supervisory initiatives, risk based supervision and the evolution of the Basel framework
Explain the progress and challenges in implementing Basel II and Basel III in India, SIFIs and compensation practices
Explain the effect of liberalisation and globalisation on monetary policy, financial markets, transparency, and international standards and codes
Explain the conditions for NBFC registration, the types of NBFC and the NBFCs regulated by other bodies
Explain the 11 activity-based categories of NBFC
Explain the growth of the NBFC sector, the Reserve Bank's regulatory powers, the three-fold focus and its developmental role
Explain the scale-based regulatory framework, PCA, auditor appointment, HFC alignment and other supervisory policies for NBFCs
Explain the evolution, objectives and eligibility conditions of primary dealers
Explain the role and responsibilities of primary dealers and the liquidity support from the Reserve Bank
Explain the performance measures, success ratio and turnover ratio of primary dealers
Explain the primary market underwriting and bidding guidelines, the secondary market, investment and HTM guidelines and capital adequacy for primary dealers
